Hi Samir - great speaking with you and Alex earlier. Below is a concise post-call recap and recommended next steps so your infra/procurement/security teams have an action list. I attached our Dedicated pricing matrix and a Private VPC checklist for reference.

Post-call recap (high level):
- Goals: low latency for interactive features, predictable throughput for peak loads, and strict data isolation for PHI workloads.
- Current stack: OpenAI for interactive + internal GPU cluster for batch. Looking to consolidate where it reduces ops burden and cost.

Deployment mode guidance:
- Hosted API: fast to start (no infra work), good for dev/proof-of-concept and low to moderate usage. Models are managed by Redwood; can be pin-pointed to a model version but not ideal if you need customer-dedicated hardware or strict network isolation.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools for predictable latency and throughput (SLA-backed). Good fit for your interactive prod traffic that needs steady response times and cost predictability. Supports the same model versions; we recommend Dedicated as the primary prod target for predictable performance.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): recommended for regulated PHI workloads requiring KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, and customer-managed networking. Some orchestration differences exist (control plane separation) but model behavior is consistent.

Migration approach (recommended):
1) Start with Hosted API for a quick POC against your interactive flows (no infra changes).
2) Run a parallel Dedicated environment (canary capacity) and mirror traffic (traffic-splitting) to validate latency, batching behavior, and cost.
3) For Private/VPC migration, prep network/VPC peering and KMS; once connectivity is validated, cut over segregated PHI workloads.

Typical timeline: POC (2-3 weeks) -> Dedicated canary (2-4 weeks) -> Private onboarding (4-8 weeks) depending on procurement and network approvals.

Attachments included: redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf, redwood-private-vpc-checklist.xlsx, sow-draft.docx

- Marissa (me) + Rishi: schedule technical deep-dive with your infra (propose Fri 6/12 or Mon 6/15)
- Stephanie: prep migration runbook draft and SOW (attached)

I'll follow up with calendar invites once you confirm the next steps.

Subject: Proposed canary + migration plan (short)

Hi Samir/Alex - looping in a short canary plan and answers to Alex's questions.

1) Region pinning: yes - both Dedicated and Private can be constrained to US-only regions. We'll note this in the SOW and network docs.

2) Model parity & quantization: the runtime supports multiple precision paths. For Dedicated we typically use FP16 or mixed precision to balance latency/cost. For Private you can opt into lower-precision quantized runtimes (int8) for cost savings; this may slightly change token-level outputs in edge cases. Recommended approach: run canary with the same precision settings you plan to use in prod and validate against your eval prompts.

3) Batch vs interactive economics: keep high-throughput, latency-tolerant batch on your internal GPU cluster during the migration to save cost; Dedicated for interactive production gives predictable latency and lower tail latencies. We can provide recommended batching/throughput settings and an estimated monthly cost split once we see your tokens/seq-length distribution.

Canary plan (proposed):
- Week 0: Hosted POC (validate functional parity).
- Week 1-2: Dedicated canary (10-20% mirrored traffic, run in US region, collect latency/cost/quality).
- Week 3-4: Ramp Dedicated to go-live for interactive; keep batch on-prem for 6-8 weeks while we optimize batching/quantization.

I'll attach a SOW snippet and migration runbook to the HubSpot deal. If this looks good, Marissa can kick off procurement and I can schedule a deep technical session with your infra team.

Thanks,
